previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of failed kidney transplant was admitted with fevers, chills, and a diffuse itchy rash that began after receiving cefazolin at dialysis for presumed catheter site infection. Evaluation revealed no evidence of active infection, and blood cultures were negative. The symptoms were attributed to a systemic allergic reaction to cefazolin, consistent with his known allergy. He developed reactive arthritis with knee pain, confirmed by arthrocentesis showing no infection or gout crystals. During dialysis, he experienced a flare of rash and left hand swelling, which improved with IV hydrocortisone, famotidine, and diphenhydramine. Dermatology diagnosed a fixed drug eruption and recommended clobetasol cream. Prednisone was started, improving his joint symptoms. A urine culture grew Proteus mirabilis, but due to lack of symptoms and poor urine output, it was considered colonization and not treated. He stabilized, completed his hospital course, and was discharged home with a short course of prednisone, increased phosphate binder dose, and instructions for rash management and antibiotic avoidance.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo male with ESRD on HD, recent AV fistula thrombectomy, HTN, 
CAD admitted with low grade fever and chills, found to have oral 
thrush.

1. Fever/thrush: On presentation, pt had low grade leukocytosis 
without shift and fever.  He denied any localizing symptoms and 
blood cultures, urine cx, and chest xray were all negative for 
infectious process.  On exam, AV fistula site was CDI and there 
were no remarkable findings with the exception of oral thrush.  
Pt denied any odynophagia or dysphagia.  Antibiotics were 
started for one day, d/ced and pt remained afebrile and 
asymptomatic.  He attended the next scheduled HD session and 
tolerated it well.  Given that pt was asymptomatic from the 
thrush candidal esophagitis was not worked up with endoscopy.  
Pt was started on Nystatin QID for thrush.  Bacterial infection 
was ruled out by time of discharge.  
.
Chronic:
1. ESRD: pt tolerated HD prior to discharge.  He will continue 
his normal MWF schedule and he will continue to HD appropriate 
medications for ACD and bone metabolism.  Pt's AVG has a good 
thrill and bruit and is CDI s/p thrombectomy.  When cleared by 
vascular, can restart dialysis through fistula and remove 
tunneled line.

f/u final blood cx
